_readme: THE SHELF — the looks the prototype ships that Relay did not have (REBRAND wave 4, agent T2).
ONE FILE, TWO READERS. `db/templates.rs` include_str!s this and seeds it by NAME (never by id,
so a church's channel foreign keys are never repointed); `src/lib/shelf.test.js` reads the same
bytes and renders every entry through the real TemplateRender. That is deliberate: the last time
a shipped design lived in two places — BUILTINS in templates.js and builtin_templates() in Rust —
they drifted by one row and a kiosk resolving template_id=4 rendered a song through a scripture
look. Two readers, one file, no parity to remember.
Every entry is in the LAYER model (`layout.layers`), because that is where the primitives the
prototype's looks are made of actually live: the `band` with its declared `members` (DECISIONS
§75), the `region` that is its own container (DECISIONS §74), and monitor-only bindings for a
stage screen. Geometry is PERCENT of the 16:9 frame; type sizes are cqw. Layer ids only have to
be unique within their own template.
WHAT IS NOT HERE, AND WHY: the prototype's other eleven starters. Nine already ship under Relay's
own names and one ships under the same name; duplicating a look an operator already has is a
shelf that is harder to read, not a shelf that is fuller. The diff is in the commit message and
the review note.
SEVEN, NOT EIGHT. `Lower Third · Scripture` left this shelf when the five coordinated families
landed: the family's keyed member takes that exact name, and two templates cannot share one —
seeds insert BY NAME, so the second is simply never inserted and an operator sees whichever got
there first. Its frozen bytes are in `retired_presets.json` so the migration can remove the old
layer-model row from installs that already have it. The remaining seven stay because no family
member can express their SHAPE: the region model has no composite, no monitor-only binding and
no way to inset a picture inside a frame. `Lower Third · Lyric` stays as the shelf's band.

templates.name: High Visibility
templates._proto: id 7 — pure black, white verse AND white reference, 8.4cqw. The one look that is not a design: it is the answer to a lit room and a cheap lens. Relay already ships a High Visibility THEME (themes.js); this is the template of the same name, which did not exist.

templates.name: Notice Board
templates._proto: id 8 — Announcement. A title in cyan over a blue gradient, the notice beneath it.
templates._kind: It derives as SCRIPTURE, and that is honest rather than a bug. A full-screen announcement and a full-screen verse are the same shape — a large line and a small one — which is the exact reason templateKind refuses to guess `preservice` (DECISIONS §78). A church points this at announcements through the content-look register (`tpl_announcement`), which is where a ROLE is declared in Relay, not derived.

templates.name: Media Frame
templates._proto: id 17 — the picture, framed on a near-black ground (side 6, pad 6), rather than bleeding to the edges the way the `media` starter does.
templates._departure: The prototype puts a caption under the picture. Relay's media fire carries media_url and NOTHING else (main.rs::fire_media — no reference, no text), so a caption layer here would be a line that is blank at every fire: a picture of a feature. It is left out until media content carries a title.

templates.name: Lower Third · Lyric
templates._proto: id 14 — `rhide:true`: a lyric band carries words and NO reference at all, because a song's reference is its title and a title under every line reads like a slide rather than a caption. Band from top 64, fill #05070C at 86%, baseline lift 5.

templates.name: SuperSource · Word right
templates._proto: id 10 — `ss:{layout:'wordright',split:30,pad:10,bord:true,bc:'#E2ECFA',plate:'sanctuary',wtpl:1}`. `split` is the CAMERA share in both arrangements, and a percentage pad resolves against WIDTH — so 10% bars eat 10/0.5625 = 17.78 points of HEIGHT. Getting either wrong overran the word region by 3x in the prototype, and the numbers here are its corrected ones.
templates._camera: The camera half (x 0..30) is not painted, because Relay does not take a camera feed — the switcher puts the picture there (DECISIONS §74). The plate fills the bars ABOVE and BELOW only; a full-frame background would hide the very feed this look exists to composite with.
templates._fill: `wtpl:1` is Classic Serif, and it is a REAL rendered template at region width, not a picture of one. templateRef names a BUILT-IN because a kiosk or OBS page has no database (DECISIONS §74).

templates.name: SuperSource · Word left
templates._proto: id 11 — `ss:{layout:'wordleft',split:30,pad:10,bord:false,plate:'warm',wtpl:7}`. Word on the left 70%, camera on the right 30%, no outline.
templates._departure: `wtpl:7` is the prototype's High Visibility, which is not one of Relay's five built-ins — and a region may only name a built-in, or the wall and the stream render different things. Built-in 2 (Stage Mono: black ground, white verse, cyan reference) is the closest built-in shape and is used instead. The High Visibility template on this same shelf cannot be the fill for exactly that reason.

templates.name: Stage · Large type
templates._proto: id 13 — rail on the RIGHT (railW 30), `next:true`, `timer:true`, clock and note off. 7cqw verse, #7FD4FF meta.
templates._zones: §5's switchable zones are not built (DECISIONS §75 records that they want the same declared-membership concept a band now has). A zone that is OFF is translated here as a layer that is not present, which is the same screen and no new machinery. The rail and the strip are shape tiles; the figures inside them are ordinary bound text.
templates._geometry: pad 3.6cqw and gap 2.4cqw are cqw on BOTH axes, so vertically they are 3.6/56.25 and 2.4/56.25 of the frame height — 6.4 and 4.27 points. The strip is 15 points of height at the bottom.
